value: error: variable length arrays are not supported in HLSL
note: The exact diagnostic the issue body quotes, matched literally. NOT `nonzero_exit`: on Windows dxc returns E_FAIL (0x80004005) for every ordinary diagnosed error, so an exit-code predicate cannot tell this apart from a syntax error, an unsupported profile, or an old release rejecting the repro for a reason that has nothing to do with the issue -- which is the invalid-probe trap. Two controls show it discriminates. (1) control-literal.hlsl is repro.hlsl with the bound changed to the plain literal `10` -- the issue's own working case -- and is run with --expect no-match; it compiles clean, so the predicate is not firing on everything. (2) case-nonarray-ice-contexts.hlsl fails to compile with THREE errors (case label, non-type template argument, enumerator) and is also run with --expect no-match, so the predicate is shown to name this diagnostic rather than 'the compile failed'. The `error: ` prefix is part of the literal so a note or a quotation of the message cannot satisfy it. Marker note: `are not supported` appears in the invalid-probe feature-absence markers, but this string is a positive `contains` clause of the issue's own predicate, so classify() suppresses the demotion -- which is exactly the diagnostic-quality-issue case SKILL.md describes.
